en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Water-Jar.
2. The Question on the Two Qualities of Iron “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘two qualities of iron should be adopted,’ which are those two qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, iron vomits up what it has well swallowed;”
In the same way, Great King, the mind of a practitioner engaged in yoga vomits up what it has drunk through wise attention (*yoniso manasikāra*).
This, Great King, is the first quality of black iron that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, once black iron has drunk water, it does not vomit it back up.

In the same way, Great King, whatever confidence has once arisen in a practitioner of yoga should not be vomited back up, thinking: “Exalted is that Blessed One, the Perfectly Enlightened One; well-proclaimed is the Dhamma; well-practiced is the Saṅgha.

Whatever knowledge has once arisen—namely, “Form is impermanent, feeling is impermanent, perception is impermanent, mental formations are impermanent, consciousness is impermanent”—that too should not be vomited back up.
This, Great King, is the second quality of black iron that should be adopted.
This too was said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God above Gods:
fixed in the noble Dhamma, attains distinction.”
"He does not tremble in manifold ways, nor in any way at all; he has attained the state of liberation.
Thus ends the second question on the hook of black iron.
